subject: Unexpected throughput drop after model swap — immediate actions
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@crucible.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@crucible.ai
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected throughput drop after model swap — immediate actions

Hi Vanessa —

We rolled the new model variant (redwood-model-v2.4 + int8 quant profile) at 08:30 PT this morning and immediately started seeing a sharp drop in throughput on our inference path. Metrics so far:
- Throughput down ~40% (requests/sec) vs baseline
- p95 latency jumped from ~260ms to ~820ms
- Error rate increased (5xx) on a small subset of requests

This is impacting our production API and a number of end users are seeing timeouts. We traced the timeline to the 08:30 deploy. Can you please:
1) Confirm whether a rollback to v2.3 is possible now;
2) Share any immediate mitigations (routing to fallback, increase pool capacity);
3) We can provide traces — attaching a small sample.

We need this prioritized; if you can put someone on it now that would be great.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Head of Platform
Crucible AI

Subject: Re: Unexpected throughput drop after model swap — immediate actions

Vanessa / team — initial triage notes from the runtime side:
- Reproduced degraded latency locally against the sample traces. The regression correlates with the int8 kernel path used by v2.4.
- Hypothesis: a kernel selection edge-case causes repeated cache misses on KV lookups in our attention implementation when sequence lengths vary. That can create CPU-side stalls which back up the request queues and look like a throughput drop.
- Error spikes (5xx) are consistent with request timeouts due to queue saturation rather than model correctness issues.

Recommended immediate options (pros/cons):
1) Emergency rollback to redwood-model-v2.3 (fastest, known-good). Pros: recovers throughput and p95; Cons: customers lose modest accuracy improvements in v2.4.
2) Apply a targeted hotpatch to quantized kernel selection (we have a candidate patch). Pros: keeps v2.4; Cons: risk & requires testing, ~30–45 minute rollout.

I'm attaching the candidate hotpatch. I can push it to a canary pool and smoke test within ~25 minutes. If we don't have buy-in for the hotpatch, we should roll back immediately.

Command to trigger rollback (automation):
  redwoodctl deploy --model redwood-model-v2.3 --env crucible-prod --force-failover

I'll hold a canary with metrics and will report back.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Aditya / Lauren — quick exec note:
- Incident: Crucible production saw a ~40% throughput drop and p95 >3x after model swap to v2.4 (int8 quant) at ~08:30 PT.
- Impact: Customer-facing API timeouts for a segment of traffic; they have high SLAs and this is a priority account (DEAL-12984).
- Cause (tentative): quantized kernel selection bug triggering KV cache thrash / queue saturation. Markus has a candidate hotpatch; rollback is also an option.

Immediate asks:
1) Approve emergency rollback if we cannot validate hotpatch within 30 minutes — customer prefers availability.
2) Approve up to $15k in one-off credits for this incident if rollback is required and downtime persists beyond 60 minutes.
3) If you want, I can escalate to the on-call exec for further sign-off; otherwise I will proceed with the remediation path agreed by Markus / Samir.

I will keep this short and will ping again with the canary results in ~30 minutes.

— Van

- We also want the postmortem and a timeline for a permanent fix for the quant path.
